transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Well, thank you, Doctor. I came in because... lately, I've been having trouble just answering simple questions. I work as a jeweler, and when a customer asks me something basic, like when a ring repair will be ready, my answer just starts going all over the place. 

I'll start out trying to answer them, but then my mind just wanders out loud. I'll go from talking about the repair to our invoices, and then somehow I'm talking about garden soil, and then mortgage papers. I can literally see them losing me, just staring at me completely confused. It's getting really frustrating, and I just need to figure out why I can't seem to keep my words straight.
When you're talking and jumping from topic to topic like that, are you aware that you're doing it while it's happening, or do you only realize it afterward when you see people's confused reactions?

I think I realize it while it's happening. Like when they ask about that ring repair, I'll actually hear myself moving from that to the invoices, and then talking about garden soil or the mortgage papers. I know it's not what they asked, and I can see them getting lost right as I'm speaking. I just can't seem to rein it back in once it starts.
Has this problem with jumping around while you're talking been happening your whole life, or did it start more recently?

No, it's definitely not something I've dealt with my whole life. This whole change really started... I guess it was not long after we took on the business mortgage. So, it's been going on for almost two years now.
Over these past two years, have you noticed any changes in your mood or energy levels, or have you been feeling more irritable, more energetic than usual, or sleeping less than you normally do?

No, I haven't been more energetic or sleeping less. It's actually kind of the opposite. My mood has just been... well, most mornings I wake up with this flat, heavy sadness. It's hard to describe, but it feels like all the color has just drained out of the house before I even leave for the shop.

When you wake up with that flat, heavy sadness in the morning, does the difficulty with your thoughts jumping around happen right away with the sadness, or does the problem with your words wandering happen even on the rare mornings when your mood feels a bit better?

Well, the jumping around with my words... it actually happens even when I'm not feeling that heavy sadness. Like, there was a stretch before the depression really settled in, when my mood was okay. I was still running my jewelry making classes and working out in the garden. But even then, my thoughts were all over the place. And... well, during that same time, for several weeks, I kept hearing these noises coming from the polishing room when no one was in there. I also couldn't shake this feeling that customers were watching the business, like, keeping tabs on us. So, yeah, the wandering thoughts were happening then, too, before the sadness really started.

During that time when you heard the noises from the polishing room and felt customers were watching the business—did your mood and energy feel different from your normal baseline, or did you feel like your usual self mood-wise while experiencing those experiences?

Like I mentioned a second ago, my mood was actually pretty normal then. I felt like my usual self. That was that stretch before the heavy sadness really settled in. I had my normal energy—I was still running my jewelry making classes and keeping up with the gardening just fine. 

It was just that, for those several weeks, I kept hearing those noises from the polishing room and worrying that customers were watching the business. But as far as my mood went during that specific time, I felt okay.

During those several weeks when you were hearing the noises from the polishing room and feeling that customers were watching the business—how many hours of sleep were you getting each night, and did you notice yourself needing less sleep than usual, or was your sleep amount pretty much normal for you?

My sleep was pretty much normal for me back then. I was getting my usual amount... probably around seven or eight hours a night. I didn't notice needing less sleep or anything like that. I just went to bed and woke up at my regular times, just like always.

During those several weeks when you were hearing the noises and worried about customers watching—were you taking on more projects or activities than you normally would, or feeling like you could accomplish more than usual, or did your activity level and drive stay pretty much the same as always?

No, my activity level stayed pretty much the same. I wasn't taking on extra projects or feeling like I had some kind of unusual drive. I was just keeping up with my regular jewelry classes and my usual gardening, like I said. I didn't feel like I could accomplish more than normal or anything like that. It was just my regular routine.

During those several weeks when you were hearing the noises from the polishing room and worried about customers watching—did you feel like your thinking was racing or unusually sharp and clear, or did your mind feel like it does most of the time?
My mind felt pretty much like it does most of the time. I didn't feel like my thoughts were racing or anything like that. It wasn't unusually sharp or clear, either. Just... normal thinking, really.

When those several weeks ended—when you stopped hearing the noises from the polishing room and the feeling that customers were watching went away—did that happen suddenly, or did it gradually fade away over time?

You know, I'm not entirely sure. I don't really remember if it was all at once or if it just kind of faded out. I just know that eventually, things went back to normal and I wasn't hearing those noises or feeling like I was being watched anymore.

When you stopped hearing those noises from the polishing room and feeling like customers were watching you—did that happen around the same time the heavy sadness started, or was there a gap in between where you felt okay before the sadness settled in?

Actually, there wasn't a gap at all. They were happening together. During the worst months of it, that heavy sadness and just... losing interest in everything... that was all going on at the exact same time I was hearing my name in the shop. It was all happening right when I felt so sure the customers were checking up on our payments. So, yeah, they were happening at the same time.

When you were hearing your name in the shop and feeling sure that customers were checking up on your payments—looking back on that time, did you feel like your mood was elevated or unusually good, or did you feel depressed and lose interest in things you normally enjoy, or did your mood feel completely normal?

Like I was just saying, my mood definitely wasn't normal, and it wasn't good or elevated either. During those worst months, that really heavy sadness and the feeling of losing interest in everything... that was all happening at the exact same time. So while I was hearing my name in the shop and feeling so sure the customers were checking up on our payments, I was also feeling incredibly depressed.

When you first started hearing your name in the shop and feeling sure customers were checking on your payments—did those experiences start at the exact same time the heavy sadness began, or did the hearing and the worried feeling about customers start before the depression kicked in?

Well, thinking back on it... the hearing things and the worrying actually started first. There was a stretch of time before the depression really settled in where I was still feeling okay—I was still running my jewelry classes and doing my gardening. But for several weeks during that time, I kept hearing those noises from the polishing room and feeling so worried that the customers were watching the business. The heavy sadness came later.

During those several weeks when you were hearing your name in the shop and worried the customers were watching—looking back on it now, would you say your mood felt low and depressed the whole time, or did you feel unusually good, energetic, or like you could do anything during any part of that period?

Well, like I was saying, my mood felt pretty normal during that first stretch. I wasn't depressed yet, and I definitely wasn't feeling unusually good or overly energetic either. I was just... normal. I was still running my jewelry classes and doing my gardening, just going about my regular life. But during those several weeks, even though my mood was fine, I was still hearing those noises from the polishing room and feeling so worried that the customers were watching the business. The depression didn't start until after that.

During those several weeks when you were hearing your name in the shop and worried the customers were watching—did you feel like you had any special abilities or insights, or feel unusually confident or important in any way, or did you feel completely like your normal self in terms of how you viewed yourself?

No, I didn't feel anything like that. I didn't feel like I had special abilities or anything. I just felt like my normal self, really... just a regular person trying to get through the day. I definitely didn't feel unusually confident or important. Like I said, I was just doing my normal stuff, making jewelry and gardening, but dealing with those noises and worries.

During those several weeks when you were hearing your name in the shop and worried the customers were watching—did you feel interested in doing your jewelry classes and gardening during that time, or had you lost interest in those things even though your mood felt normal?

Well, during those first few weeks when the noises and worries started, I was still doing my classes and gardening. I was still interested in them then. But... lately, it's completely different. I used to really enjoy hunting for vintage clasps and putting together the lesson plans for my jewelry classes, but now... I just don't care. I'll sit there and stare at the trays of materials, and I just feel like there's no point in even starting. I've completely lost the drive to do any of it.

Looking back at those several weeks when you were hearing your name in the shop and worried the customers were watching—during that time, did you feel like things were going especially well for you, or like you had more confidence or optimism than usual, even though your mood wasn't depressed?

No, not at all. I didn't feel like things were going especially well... I mean, I was pretty stressed out about the customers watching and those noises, so I definitely didn't have more confidence or optimism than usual. I was just feeling... regular, I guess. Just my normal self, trying to get through the work day.

During those several weeks when you were hearing your name in the shop and worried about customers watching—looking back on it now, did you feel more hopeful, more talkative, or like you had more energy than you normally do, or did your energy and mood feel pretty much like your baseline?

No, I didn't feel more hopeful or talkative. And I definitely didn't have more energy. Like I was saying, my mood and energy were just... pretty much at my baseline. I was just trying to manage the shop and deal with all the distractions. So no, nothing like that.
